title.narrative: Emergency winterization assistance to mitigate the impact of winter weather on IDPs, returnees and non-displaced persons.

description.narrative: ltpgtIn the third year of the war, continuous constant attacks, destruction of civilian infrastructure, and uncontrolled shifting front lines are forcing people to flee in search of safer places to live and seriously worsen the lives of those who remain.ltbrgtThe project is of an emergency nature. Its main objective is to provide time-critical winterization assistance to vulnerable conflict-affected people in communities near the front line and the russian border to ensure warm, safe, and dignified living conditions during the winter season. These needs cannot be met on their own due to the ongoing war, destruction of civil infrastructure to varying degrees, lack of resources/markets and transportation capacity, and loss of income or low level, etc.ltbrgtDeveloping project NW used information provided by UHF 2024 1st RA Strategy, Ukraine SNFI Cluster Winter Plan 2024-2025 and Ukraine 2024 HNRP, statistics and results of own assessment in the target location.ltbrgtThe received information has been processed and has allowed us to determine needs, types of assistance, project locations, and the number of beneficiaries.ltbrgtThe proposed activities are:ltbrgt- prepositioning and distribution of the solid fuel to 600 HHs in Pokrovskyi and Kramatorskyi rayons of Donetska, Nikopolskyi and Kryvorizkyi rayons of Dnipropetrovska, Chuhuivskyi rayon of Kharkivska, Okhtyrskyi rayon of Sumska oblastsltbrgt- prepositioning and distribution of 1000 NFI kits in Pokrovskyi and Kramatorskyi rayons of Donetska, Nikopolskyi and Kryvorizkyi rayons of Dnipropetrovska, Chuhuivskyi rayon of Kharkivska, Okhtyrskyi rayon of Sumska oblasts.ltbrgtThe total number of people reached by assistance is 2080 individuals, incl. 272 PwD.ltbrgtThe targeted population will be people affected by the war (IDPs, non-displaced, returnees). Among them, we prioritize the elderly, PwD, large families, families with no or low income, and single households, but not limited to other vulnerable groups, which the re-verification process will confirm. ltbrgtThe proposed interventions align with the Allocation Strategy, HRP 2024 Strategic objectives, and Cluster Objectives, in particular, CO2: Deliver emergency shelter and NFI assistance mitigating the impacts of harsh winter weather for IDPs, returnees, and non-displaced people while minimizing environmental impact.ltbrgtNEW WAY (NW) is a national NGO that has supported affected people since 2016. To supplement the resources of each partner and provide comprehensive assistance, the project will be implemented in partnership with local NGO ChF "East Ukrainian Diaspora" (EUD). More information on partners can be found in the Programming tab.ltbrgtNW will be the leading agency with the following duties:ltbrgt- overall coordination and management of the project implementationltbrgt- procurement, delivering and distributing solid fuel in Donetska and Kharkivska oblastsltbrgt- procurement, delivering and distributing NFI kits in Donetska, Sumska and Kharkivska oblastsltbrgt- monitoring the progress of the project implementation and evaluating results ltbrgt- reporting to UHF and Cluster.ltbrgtWithin the framework of the project, EUD will perform the following duties:ltbrgt- conducting a needs assessment, collecting and verification of beneficiaries' personal data in Dnipropetrovska oblastltbrgt- distributing NFI kits in Dnipropetrovska oblastltbrgt- procurement, delivering and distributing solid fuel in Dnipropetrovska oblastltbrgt- processing of primary documentation after distributionltbrgtThe Log Frame tab provides more information on partners' obligations. Both NGOs are aware of the local context and humanitarian principles.ltbrgtPotential risks have been analyzed, and mitigation measures have been elaborated. lt/pgt
